criteria.reasoning: The memo finds the double posting of Priyanka Desai's $250 gift (G-41817 and G-41822 against one PayBridge transaction). But its adjusting entry reads "Delete G-41817, the automatic import; keep G-41822." The criterion requires deleting G-41822 and says to FAIL if G-41817, the posting tied to the PayBridge transaction, is deleted instead.

The memo's discrepancy #2 states that G-41809 (Marisol Etxeberria, check 4410) was keyed as $15,000.00 while the bank item in RDC-0710-1 is $1,500.00. It corrects the gift amount to $1,500.00, a $13,500.00 reduction, and does not delete or reverse the gift. This meets the criterion.

The memo says of the Etxeberria correction: "The acknowledgment sent 2026-07-13 can stand; her calendar-year giving statement in January will show the corrected $1,500.00." That leaves the $15,000 acknowledgment in place and defers the correction to a later statement, which is the FAIL condition.

The memo identifies Hollis Grant's $500 check 2231 (G-41810) as returned NSF on 2026-07-16. However, its adjusting entry reads "Delete G-41810 from B-2607-02, since the money never cleared." The criterion says to FAIL if the memo deletes the original gift instead of posting a -$500 reversing entry that keeps the original on record. The memo does not post a reversal dated July 16.

Discrepancy #4 identifies G-41803, check 9014 for $1,000 from Gerald & Mae Lindgren, received 2026-07-02 but postmarked 2026-06-30, as an FY2026 gift. It re-dates the gift to 2026-06-30 and moves it to B-2606-YE. The adjustment removes $1,000 from the July total. This meets every element of the criterion.

The memo correctly leaves G-41802 (Doyle) in July, but it moves G-41804 (Ochieng, check 1187) to FY2026: "Re-date to 2026-06-28 and move it to B-2606-YE." The criterion says to FAIL if either gift is moved to FY2026 or re-dated to the check date.

The memo states that card gifts are $3,335.00 gross and PayBridge paid out $3,257.13 net, with the $77.87 difference being PayBridge's fee (2.2% + $0.30 per transaction). It calls this "expected", keeps gifts at gross, and says "No CRM entry." It does not call the difference an error or shortfall. The $77.87 goes to 6120 Merchant fees in the GL, not the CRM, which is acceptable. The Section 1 table shows a $250 card difference, but that is the duplicate gift, not the fee, and it is resolved in Section 2.

The memo states "Card gifts are $3,335.00 gross; PayBridge paid out $3,257.13 net across 13 payouts. The $77.87 difference is PayBridge's fee" and books $77.87 to 6120 Merchant fees. The tie-out repeats the $77.87 figure. This matches the criterion, and no other fee total appears.

The memo says: "Valley Office Supply, $86.40 (check 33817, item 5 of RDC-0724-1): a vendor refund, not a gift. Do not enter it in the CRM; Finance codes it in the general ledger." The corrected batch total of $16,880.00 does not include it. The $86.40 shows up only as a reconciling item in the bank tie-out, not as a gift. That matches the criterion.

The memo states the corrected July batch total as $16,880.00. The criterion requires $17,130.00 and lists $16,880.00 as a failing figure. The memo moved the Ochieng check (G-41804, $250) to FY2026 in addition to the other four adjustments, which is why its total is lower.

Section 4 ties the corrected total of $16,880.00 to the bank net of $18,123.53. It lists PayBridge fees (−$77.87), the Lindgren check (+$1,000.00), and the Valley Office Supply refund (+$86.40) as reconciling items, and it states "Unexplained difference $0.00." The arithmetic checks out.
